transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-07 16:00 UTC | Duration 43m | Attendees: Maya, Jon, Avery (Redwood); Rita, Samir, Leah, Tony (EmberPoint)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run about 40 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:06] Rita: Rita here, sorry running a bit late, all good.
[00:09] Samir: Samir on platform.
[00:11] Leah: Leah from product.
[00:12] Tony: Tony infra.
[00:14] Maya: great, jon is going to walk through the audit logging flow and retention knobs we discussed. jon?
[00:20] Jon: yeah thanks. so quick recap: for this pilot we default to hosted inference with VPC peering to your infra, we keep two levels of logs — request-level metadata and full transcript logs which are optional and configurable. the current UI shows retention at 30/90/365 days.
[00:36] Rita: can you spell out where those logs live? are they in your control plane or forwarded into our S3?
[00:41] Jon: good q; by default they stay in our control plane for the hosted plan but we have an export path — you can push them to a customer-owned S3 via IAM role. i showed that briefly in the last session, today i'll demo the export job.
[00:58] Samir: and the KV cache — sorry KV cash, uh cache — is any of that persisted in logs? i want to make sure we aren't leaking secrets into logs.
[01:07] Jon: no persistent kv values are excluded by default. we mask certain tokens and any key-material is redacted. that said there's a small window in transient logs; we recommend using our prefix cache only when you flip on advanced redaction config.
[01:23] Rita: what about SSO? we wanted to test Okta woven in; mapping groups to roles for audit.
[01:29] Maya: yep, Okta SAML is supported. next steps would be a test window where you add the sandbox Okta app and we validate group mappings.
[01:36] Tony: any quirks? our SSO team likes to have SCIM provisioning too.
[01:40] Jon: we don't do full SCIM in pilot—it's on the roadmap. for now you can do SAML assertions and we support just-in-time group mapping via attributes. provisioning we can simulate with a CSV user seed.
[01:53] Leah: is there MFA enforced on the Redwood console? our security policy is req MFA for admin users.
[01:57] Maya: MFA is enforced via your IdP (Okta). we enforce session timeouts and support conditional access via Okta policies.
[02:06] Rita: about audit logs — i need a schema. fields, timezones, event types, user identity. can you share a sample?
[02:13] Jon: yes, i'll export a sample CSV with columns: event_time, event_type, user_id, route, model_id, token_count, status, request_id. note that transcript field is optional and may be in a separate object.
[02:28] Samir: timezone handling? we want everything normalized to UTC.
[02:31] Jon: all events are stored in UTC. exports include timezone header but values are UTC.
[02:36] Rita: retention policy reversibility — if we choose 30 days, can we backfill older logs for a compliance audit later?
[02:43] Jon: once logs are deleted from hosted retention they're gone; that's why we recommend exporting to your S3 if you need long-term retention. we do have a short hold window for deletion requests but it's not a long-term archive.
[02:56] Leah: ok that aligns.
[02:58] Maya: jon can you run the demo now?
[03:00] Jon: yup, i'll share my screen — please shout if audio cuts.
[03:05] [demo noise, screen share indicated]
[03:20] Jon: here in the console under Settings -> Logs, you can toggle transcript capture per-route. i'm turning on transcript capture for the '/assistant' route to show export.
[03:32] Jon: starting export job, it's queued. on the right is the export config: S3 destination, prefix, IAM role, gzip option, retention tag.
[03:42] Tony: will the export include raw JSON of the request?
[03:45] Jon: yes, by default it is JSON; we also offer CSV flattening for analytics teams. raw JSON will have request and response, but transcripts are redacted if redaction is enabled.
[03:58] Rita: what about encryption-at-rest and KMS? our policy requires customer-managed keys.
[04:03] Jon: we support customer KMS keys for S3 exports; for hosted control plane we use server-side encryption with keys we manage, but we can arrange an enterprise contract to support bring-your-own-key for the control plane in Private mode.
[04:20] Rita: that could be a stopper. we need to see a doc outlining options.
[04:24] Maya: i'll attach the KMS options doc after the call (security-pack.pdf).
[04:28] Samir: SOC2 — do you have Type II? and can we get the evidence package?
[04:32] Maya: yes we have SOC2 Type II for the platform; i'll send the report plus a mapped evidence matrix showing which controls map to which artifacts.
[04:40] Leah: for data residency our primary ask is EU-region hosting for EU customers. are exports region-locked?
[04:47] Jon: exports go to the S3 bucket region you specify. hosted inference region selection is available — you can pin model serving to eu-west-1 for the pilot.
[04:57] Rita: incident response — do you provide audit trails for execs and longer retention for forensics?
[05:02] Jon: we can increase retention on-demand for investigations but again that's easier if you manage exports. we also support per-request debug logs that include stack traces but those are gated by an elevated token.
[05:15] Tony: how about log integrity — do you sign logs or offer WORM storage?
[05:19] Jon: we don't currently sign logs, but if you export to S3 we can provide guidance for Object Lock / WORM with S3 governance.
[05:29] Rita: good. i wanted to raise one more thing — our legal team will want the data deletion flow for subject access requests (SAR). can you walk that through?
[05:37] Maya: sure. SARs: if a user requests deletion, we can delete user-level entries and scrub transcripts upon request. we have an API for targeted deletions and a process for deletion audit.
[05:49] Samir: is the deletion immediate across caches and kv?
[05:52] Jon: immediate for control plane stores; for edge caches there can be a short TTL before it's purged. we document the TTL per deployment.
[06:02] [brief pause, background chair squeak]
[06:08] Leah: on the SOC2 mapping, can you mark which controls require dedicated Dedicated or Private deployments?
[06:14] Maya: yes i'll map each control and flag material differences — e.g., BYOK is only available in Private or enterprise Dedicated contracts.
[06:24] Rita: what's the plan for the Okta test?
[06:26] Maya: suggest a 45-minute window next week. jon will be on to validate SAML assertions and group mapping.
[06:34] Tony: we need to ensure service accounts are provisioned ahead of time.
[06:37] Maya: we'll send a checklist.
[06:40] Jon: one more demo note — when you export transcripts there's an option to pseudonymize PII via our redaction engine. it's not perfect, but it helps for analytic exports.
[06:51] Rita: is pseudonymization reversible? we need to be careful for legal holds.
[06:55] Jon: it's reversible only if you retain the mapping keys; if you want irreversible hashing we can do that too. we can document tradeoffs.
[07:05] Leah: ok, so to recap can we list specific deliverables?
[07:09] Maya: sure: 1) Jon will share sample audit log export and run a short export demo into a sandbox S3 (due 4/14). 2) Maya will send SOC2 Type II + pen test artifacts (due 4/9). 3) Customer to confirm Okta test window and provision service account (due 4/13).
[07:27] Rita: works for me.
[07:29] Samir: same. quick Q — any blockers on our end for retention testing?
[07:33] Jon: only that you provide S3 bucket + IAM role for pilot export; we need a role ARN.
[07:40] Tony: will send role ARN by EOD tomorrow.
[07:44] Maya: perfect.
[07:46] [rough cross-talk about scheduling]
[08:02] Maya: okay we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and calendar invite for the Okta test. thanks all.
[08:10] Rita: thanks everyone.
[08:12] [meeting ends]

Notes: There are minor transcription artifacts ("KV cash" and occasional label jitter). Shared artifacts referenced: security-pack.pdf (link will be emailed), sample-audit-export.csv (to be shared), SOC2-TypeII-redwood.pdf.

Recap (end): agreed next steps and owners; primary risk noted: BYOK/control-plane KMS for hosted vs private, customer to evaluate BYOK needs for compliance.
